notes.title: DevUpdate: Fabrics
notes.content:
[p]Hello to all fans of building, modeling, and creating!
[/p][p]In this Steampost I’d like to show you something I actually added quite a while ago, but which still brings me just as much joy![/p][p][/p][p]Some of you keen-eyed observers may have already spotted it in screenshots before. I’m talking about objects made out of fabric! That means all sorts of flags, pennants, banners… as well as tents and market stalls![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/b0b099baa876414e7b9c6830b9fcbfdd81e9bd59.gif"][/img][/p][p]Each of these lets you customize the fabric, its color, pattern, and even symbols.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/babaf1859c52da36c3854825d01644d165448e51.gif"][/img][/p][p]
On top of that, I’ve added a whole palette of various carpets, so you can break up the monotony of large, uniform floors.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/3682edee01262c2dadbd6832d5c2561ee5ada83e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Or, for example, decorate the inside of a tent![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/88b44c8bc21aca7c16c04a473100bc4b96fb7472.jpg"][/img][/p][p]These decorations are really cool and have become some of the objects I use most often. You’ll get to see that for yourself in the new trailer I’ll be publishing next week!  Take care, and keep an eye out for the next Steamposts! 
[/p][p][b]P.S.[/b] Of course, the flags & tents models will only be available in the full [b]1.0 release[/b] and won’t appear in the upcoming demo.[/p]

notes.title: DevUpdate: Bridges
notes.content:
[p]Hello to all fans of building, modeling, and creating![/p][p]Finally, the moment has come when I can present to you some exciting new content I’ve added to [b]Outside the Blocks[/b]![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/1b206592e559e015e9686a004c70cf189ad3c7d8.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]First up… [b]BRIDGES![/b] Below you’ll find a few images showcasing the results of my tests.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/49c6756cfc630e9dcea3c4bc994da41a21dbfdf4.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/32c2321afb57dc7ced4eb9edeaa55214b97b42ab.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The game now features 4 bridge modules that can be combined in all sorts of different ways, along with a variety of materials.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/94c9f44a525cc4bec8d1bb011d0e3e58a05ca60e.gif"][/img][/p][p]Another cool feature is that you can freely connect them with architectural modules, creating all kinds of unique and amazing constructions.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/7700d03bc4f466f85912d96f8b7bb2d19110ca8b.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]I hope you already have thousands of ideas in your heads for how to make use of these modules! I can’t wait to see what you’ll build with them.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/04f8a67ffc385f58d33f079b9782fa803c961ffe.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]P.S.[/b] Of course, the bridge models will only be available in the full [b]1.0 release[/b] and won’t appear in the upcoming demo.[/p]

notes.title: DevUpdate: Beta Celebration!
notes.content: [p]Hello to all fans of building, modeling, and creating![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/aa465a2d3a2d8f20e1191ba3a820b8f16df7a044.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This weekend, to celebrate reaching Beta of [i]Outside the Blocks[/i], I decided to take a short holiday and… visit another open-air museum! This time it was the Muzeum Kultury Ludowej Pogórza Sudeckiego.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/0a5c4cd5201270616fbeb8bd478ae8911178f694.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/e043fb8c57a50a3f1ccae617d7e5cd13e296c663.jpg"][/img][/p][p]My plan was to look at everything carefully and check whether I had missed anything in the game![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/7c4dbf55732f7c34eac2d0f86efb2252671545fa.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/109e703c18c7b901f4056626d9834e89ac38c8b4.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/0b89b636d684c2b89abaa0517b942cd3a0fa7778.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I think my mission was a success, because pretty much everything I found could be recreated![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/91bcc82dfd316f4fce2cd1293a99720d4d096a85.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/b1699306c19cee4f0a2abba3adef7bfcd96c650e.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/947acae518132ed74abc915e465d92c7854cde2c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/e37607cd1c80e6c433d7517755967105cedaca4d.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/620f5eb201e3be7f9cc1be720028148e55e908a6.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/4b33465c6fda8e1390c36d966a48dd285bc00d47.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/cb3967dbb151a09f069e1967ee28cbe6bb5d961f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The only exception was a really awesome bell tower. Maybe, if I find some extra time, I’ll add it before the official release![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/92ff99ce22c692d340948bb167687ec10a1fa451.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I hope you also had a great weekend! [/p][p]See you in the next Steam post![/p]

notes.title: The game is ready!
notes.content: [p]I’ll keep it short and straight to the point: [/p][h1][b]OUTSIDE THE BLOCKS IS DONE![/b][/h1][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/5d1f01a2cc6904f8ceabb5672c01ddad4943e584.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]What does that mean?[/h2][p]I’ve finished all the planned work needed to release [i]Outside the Blocks[/i]. The game now has the full set of features and content to be in your hands![/p][p][/p][h2]Does that mean it’s releasing tomorrow?[/h2][p]Not yet. I want you to get a polished and comfortable product, so in the coming weeks I’ll focus on fine-tuning, adding some quality-of-life improvements, and fixing any bugs that still show up.[/p][p][/p][h2]Can I help with testing?[/h2][p]Absolutely! This September I’m planning to release a new [b]DEMO[/b], which you’ll be able to [b]PLAY[/b] and [b]REVIEW [/b]on Steam. Your feedback will play a huge role in determining how soon the full release happens![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/c7a7ac562933dc55b08d6d4443f63c0274d1edfc.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]What’s in the demo?[/h2][p]The new demo is aimed mostly at players who haven’t tried [i]Outside the Blocks[/i] yet, but veteran feedback is just as important.[/p][p]Here’s what’s new:[/p][list][*][p][b]Features:[/b] Undo/Redo, light sources, animated objects, and more[/p][/*][*][p][b]Improvements:[/b] reworked tutorial, new material system, revamped camera controls[/p][/*][*][p][b]Content:[/b] a slightly smaller set of objects than in the old demo, but with fresh additions[/p][/*][/list][p]Since I’m developing this game completely solo, it’s easy to get biased or miss obvious issues. That’s why your feedback is invaluable.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/4fc00bea17cfd688a0a3e61de95c171ab95200d3.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]What’s next?[/h2][p]Stay tuned for updates and new posts where I’ll showcase what’s coming in the final version. I’ve got plenty of cool stuff I can’t wait to share with you soon![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/40cc0f16cf8246fd7dee35e542160ab4bcace037.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Take care and see you in next steam post! [/p]

notes.title: DevUpdate: 1.0 Animals
notes.content:
Hello to all fans of building, modeling, and creating!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/90ca8d7481f1f33a0cc63e6ac381e6811f44ca7d.jpg[/img]

Taking advantage of these last few moments while I still have a chair and a computer in front of me (I’m moving, and my workspace is in total chaos), I wanted to tell you a bit about the animals that will be available in version 1.0!

[h1]Demo Animals[/h1]
In one of the previous Steam posts, I already mentioned that animated animals are big part of OtB. If you haven’t read it yet, I highly encourage you to check it out!
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2350220/view/4690026640910991183
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/11ad815a9781b2e3173ba098f7dfac798349dae0.gif[/img]

The demo included 5 farm animal models, and it seems like you had a great time building dioramas with them. While browsing your creations, I got the strange feeling that hiding chickens in weird places has somehow become an unplanned meta-game. ːbrownchickenː

[h1]New Animals[/h1]
Originally, I planned for about 12 animal models in the final game. But seeing how excited you all were, I decided to go the extra mile. In Outside the Blocks version 1.0, there will be a whopping... 38 types of animals, most of them available in several poses or animation sets!
Yep, that’s over three times more than I originally planned, but looking at the final results, I’m convinced it was worth it!

[h2]🐄 Domesticated Animals[/h2]
In addition to the farm animals from the demo, there are some new ones, characteristic of medieval rural areas and farmsteads.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/26bd9fdd02727a981b4dea50b3152f8cfcf6c28d.gif[/img]

[h2]🐻 Wild Animals[/h2]
The wild forest animal selection has been expanded the most. I’m especially excited that you can now create entire animal families roaming around together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/8219271e6c064706a60d3c5f9daea9d53d0192ec.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/e4b069320d53b4e2132384f77f4c10fd52732661.gif[/img]

[h2]🐦 Birds[/h2]
Birds turned out to be a really nice touch that adds to the atmosphere. Several of them have recently been implemented.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/387f3230d0f9ec84cdaae68e87b8e09e1cbff706.gif[/img]

[h2]🐟 Fish[/h2]
Many people asked me about adding fish, so here they are! Perfect whether you're making a seaside scene, a pond, or even an aquarium.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/610d75874a98cbdeb53783114809b0e603594614.gif[/img]

[h2]🦋 Butterflies[/h2]
Nobody asked for butterflies, but I don’t care. I wanted to add them anyway!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/ea7ab6c99abf9703cfbf4dd873bc68f6f116516f.gif[/img]

A small extra touch: when you move the spawner, they fly toward its center.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/1e4a128843a4a849040acf0be595819dbd1d02dd.gif[/img]

[h1]To sum it up...[/h1]
I think there's now enough variety for everyone to express their creativity, no one should feel left out!
These past few weeks of development have been very intense. I’ve added tons of awesome new content, and I can't wait to show you more! I'm planning to post dev updates more regularly from now on.
In the meantime, feel free to join our Discord, where I share more behind-the-scenes stuff:

👉 https://discord.com/invite/mAYsGS77t3

See you soon! Hopefully after I’ve finished moving!

[b]P.S.[/b]
I’m working hard to share the game with more communities. I’d love to hear how you first discovered it, let me know in the comments!

notes.title: DevUpdate: Light emiting objects
notes.content:
Hello to all fans of building, modeling, and creating!

I’m dropping in with the first update since the roadmap went live, and let me just say – seeing Outside the Blocks getting more attention lately has been amazing. The growing interest, the shares, the mentions… it really keeps me motivated. Thank you! ːespressoː

Also – fun fact – just a few weeks ago, the demo hit a new peak in player count, which is absolutely incredible considering it’s just a small demo!

As for the development timeline: Everything is moving forward as planned. Not too fast, not too slow, but steady. And today, I want to show off something I quietly wrapped up a few weeks ago…

[h2]Light-emitting objects
[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/c311ebbedaf5db743c41495f7fe2f09a7d1ed009.jpg[/img]
Yes – they’re here, and they’re glowing. This has been one of the most requested features, and I totally get why – lighting changes everything.

Right now, you can use several types of light sources, including:
[list]
[*] Campfire
[*] Torches
[*] Braziers
[*] Standing torches
[*] And of course… candles
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/d4b7f8f266f86106b34b2ce2d372b2300db10fa8.gif[/img]

It’s kind of wild how much light transforms a scene. A quiet evening setting becomes warm and alive. A spooky forest? Actually spooky. I hope this sparks tons of ideas for your dioramas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/a580f2888f264163ad6decf4e951f8116a59e743.jpg[/img]
And yep – each light object can be turned ON or OFF. Want to show the same location at two different times of day? Or a moment before and after the fire’s been lit? You’ve got full control.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/f0b5c58cd050db3e703dc820a30c541b08dfe026.gif[/img]

Honestly, this might be one of the coolest features in the game so far. They influence every object within the scene.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/18118321ba8c864e1defd20673e638a8f1824a19.gif[/img]

And it also affects all weather effects, like fog!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/0a7a2d1c154bcb1d1d908b2a44ec5871a296d966.gif[/img]

Of course, this is just one of the new features I’ve added recently. If you want to follow development more closely, hop into our Discord:
https://discord.gg/5vjajYwR

And hey… if you haven’t played the demo yet, now’s a good time. No one really knows how long it’ll be up on Steam, so grab it while you can.

Take care, and keep an eye out for the next update!

notes.title: Road to 1.0 & Future Plans
notes.content:
Hello to all the fans of building, modeling, and creating!

The Outside the Blocks demo has been available for a while now! 
[b]Thank you to everyone who played[/b] – and especially to those who shared their feedback!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/06262b93d54f316785550711dccc46a7b49a21da.jpg[/img]

Looking at your comments and activity on Steam, it seems like the demo has been well received – which, I must admit, makes me really happy!

The interest in Outside the Blocks is greater than I expected, but unfortunately, it's still not big enough for me to turn this project into anything more than a hobby project developed in my spare time. Because of that, [b]I plan to continue working on the game in the same way as before.[/b]
The good news is – this won’t significantly affect the content of the final game. 
The bad news? The release will be delayed. By how much? No one knows. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/3759c89813e0ecf01a9b336f7c92fbf493ea2bdb.jpg[/img]
[h1]Regarding version 1.0 – there will be a lot of new content![/h1]
Here are some of the features planned for version 1.0. Keep in mind that this list may still change.

[h2]New Features:
[/h2]
[list]
[*] Undo / Redo
[*] Expanded customization of the display stand base
[*] Material Workspace rework
[*] Weather Workspace rework
[*] Improvements to Autobuild usability
[*] Optimization
[*] Various QoL (Quality of Life) improvements
[/list]
[h2]New Customization Options:[/h2]
[list]
[*] New Glass Presets
[*] New Display Cases (various sizes and shapes)
[*] New Substance Presets
[*] New Terrain Presets
[*] New Atmospheric Effects
[*] New Lighting Schemes
[/list]
[h2]New Autobuild Modules:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Terraces & Stairs
[*] Stone Flooring
[*] Bridge
[*] New Wall Styles in Autobuild
[*] New Roof Finishing Options
[/list]
[h2]New Material Presets[/h2]
[list]
[*] Brick materials
[*] Stone materials
[*] Floors
[/list]
[h2]New Objects & Decorations:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Small Architecture Elements
[*] New Dormer Windows
[*] New Decorative Objects
[*] New Animated Farm Animals
[*] Animated Characters
[*] Animated Wild Animals
[*] Movable Objects
[*] Light-Emitting Objects
[*] Flags & Banners
[*] Stone Fences
[*] Round Tower Elements
[*] Cultivated Plants
[*] Ivy and Vines
[/list]
As you can see from the list above, I’m currently [b]focusing solely on the Medieval decoration kit.[/b] In the future, I may expand OtB with additional thematic kits, but that depends on many factors, and it’s too early to discuss it now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/4a7760e0938276b22e879e8454bd58551f453861.jpg[/img]

[h1]Regarding other frequently asked topics:[/h1]

[h2]Still Under Consideration:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Gamepad support
[*] Steam Workshop integration
[/list]
[h2]Maybe in the Future:
[/h2]
[list]
[*] Additional language versions
[*] Ability to share dioramas with other users
[*] Console versions
[/list]
[h2]Definitely Not Planned:
[/h2]
[list]
[*] Export to graphic formats (FBX, OBJ, STL) & Integration with any 3D software or game engine
I know that many people have already asked for an export feature, but I can't provide it. It's not due to technical limitations, but for legal reasons. So, there’s no room for discussion. :(

[*] Object scaling and rotation along a different axis than the vertical one
It's against my philosophy of creating and placing assets.

[*] iOS, Linux
Making a separate build is time-consuming and requires a lot of work. I just can't afford it. 

[*] VR, AR
Preparing such a version is an incredible amount of work that would never have a chance to pay off.

[*] Interiors
That would complicate navigation through the scene too much.
[/list]

I want the development process to be as transparent as possible, so in the coming months, I will regularly share WIP updates on Discord. If you want to see how the game grows and evolves – join our server!

I hope you have a great time in the demo, and I’ll catch you in the next Steam post!

notes.title: Crafting Authentic Medieval Mood
notes.content:
Regarding references, I previously talked a bit about terrain, and now it's time to share the story of the heart of every diorama – the buildings!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/3fe131a3756f8415e89dde8e849113e633ea7783.png[/img]
As you've probably noticed, I have a deep passion for medieval architecture. It's a subject that has fascinated me for many years. So, it's hard to say that when working on Outside the Blocks, I did any research because, in reality, this research has been a lifelong endeavor. Wherever I go, if I encounter an open-air museum or an old town, I always make sure to carefully observe and document what I see.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/764baef2e010779ff23029aba00d4adf97a3ab20.jpg[/img]
One of the most amazing places I've had the opportunity to visit was Troyes – a small town in France renowned for its beautifully preserved timber-framed buildings. In fact, Troyes became one of the key inspirations when I was working on the modular system in OtB!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/e9e561102c24b379d85708a0b583a6d6327ca6dd.png[/img]
In designing the building blocks, I gathered 1,750 references of interesting buildings, which I meticulously analyzed and broke down into appropriate modules. I can confidently say that the vast majority of them could easily be reconstructed my game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/f4c95dadfccd2744b328f2b256b76c45c73871e5.png[/img]
Of course, Outside the Blocks wouldn't be complete without captivating props and small-scale architecture. For this, I drew inspiration from visits to Polish open-air museums that document everyday life from various historical periods. I’m sure many of you, looking at these photos, will immediately associate them with The Witcher.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/46e3b1330de0889de94fa0af3c35a2fb6550149b.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/f552b583d1fa9b48040da9b396c5462d381276dc.png[/img]
I’ve already managed to model some of these elements, but there are still plenty that are patiently waiting in the backlog.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/0deeaf7c884c61b63b9a28dcf9464680515ed338.png[/img]
I hope you share my love for the medieval era, and that you’ll have a blast designing your own dioramas – something I’m excited to see happening very soon!

notes.title: DevUpdate: Playtests
notes.content:
Hello to all the fans of building, modeling, and creating!

I need to update you on the current situation because, even though not much time has passed since the last post, a lot has happened. Really, a lot!

Let me start by saying that last month I wrapped up the first version of the demo. I was very pleased with the result and sent it to a professional tester.

However, my enthusiasm didn’t last very long. A few days later, I received a gameplay recording. That video turned out to be the most emotional footage I’ve ever seen in my life, and trust me, I’ve seen a lot of movies. The death of Mufasa, the opening of Finding Nemo, or Up were all incredibly impactful on me, but none of them could compare to the video showing someone’s first interaction with Outside the Blocks. I’ll admit it openly: during the scene where the tester spent 30 minutes struggling to place a simple window, more than one tear rolled down my cheeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/617df7f0f44469a3e3e4af363806a39eb9002ffd.gif[/img]

The tester’s final review was rather lukewarm. While the visuals were appreciated, many aspects seemed unclear, and several features were never discovered at all.
That was the moment I realized there was still quite a bit of work ahead of me. I made a detailed list of all the problems and minor bugs, which totaled slightly over 30 items. Naturally, I addressed and fixed every single one of them, but the biggest upgrade was yet to come.

I needed to add a tutorial.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/7d35efafcf80c42c496f35a0d63da3e84c42298f.jpg[/img]
[h3]Wow! The game needs a tutorial — what a surprise?!
[/h3]
Well, no, it wasn’t a huge surprise. But honestly, I’d been holding out hope for a long time that the game would stand on its own. I always wanted Outside the Blocks to be so intuitive and simple that it wouldn’t require any explanation. I wanted every player to look at the icons and say, “Got it, let’s build some dioramas.”
And surely, there will be players like that! But I didn’t want my reluctance to stop players who prefer to understand something before they start playing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/23a6a6a3f49fc1ccfc6f482821939b4413571bed.jpg[/img]
I worked on the tutorial nonstop for over a week.

A few days ago, I sent it to a small group of people to see how it fared this time. And… it’s hard to describe what happened as anything other than a success! The general feedback seems much more positive:

[i]The game is more complex than I thought it would be based on the video, but that’s because it offers so many possibilities.[/i]

There were 2-3 points where the instructions were less clear than they should have been, and a few minor bugs were found. It looks like no major overhauls are needed anymore. I’m moving forward, analyzing, learning, and improving. Hopefully, I’ll be able to release the demo to the public soon.

Keep your fingers crossed, and see you in the next Steam post!

notes.title: DevUpdate: Animals
notes.content:
Hello to all fans of building, modeling, and creating!

I’ve got some exciting news to share!
Animated animals are now part of Outside the Blocks! This feature has been on my list for ages, and I’m thrilled to finally see it come to life. Here’s Peter the Pig in his natural habitat (alongside some friends)!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/d1c575647b483acb6e2b051c6a4d3a8809f6b0e6.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/11ad815a9781b2e3173ba098f7dfac798349dae0.gif[/img]

Initially, I wanted them to walk around the parcel, but after a few tests, I found that keeping the animals stationary better fits the game’s vision. Adding full movement felt like it would push Outside the Blocks toward creating an entire ecosystem or simulation, which isn’t the direction I’m aiming for. Instead, precision in placing each element is key, allowing everyone to showcase their own creative ideas rather than random or chaotic scenes.

What I do think fits perfectly into these miniature worlds, however, is giving each animal a choice of animations and poses. The options are limited for now, but I’ll keep working to expand them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/5837fc7bc62c2e29a17566718fe00d4604179fc1.gif[/img]

I’m really happy with how creatures bring scenes to life! Currently, I’ve mainly added farm animals, including:

[list]
[*] Pig,
[*] Sheep,
[*] Cow,
[*] Goat,
[*] Chicken!
[/list]
My goal is to add more animals over time. Next up, I’m thinking of a goose and maybe a couple of woodland creatures — a wild boar, perhaps? Or maybe a moose or a bear?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/38dcee7f316a23ce3addfd2edfa1b9da4f47c48f.gif[/img]

Are there any animals you’d love to add to your diorama?
Let me know in the comments, and see you in the next Steam post!

notes.title: References: Terrain Presets
notes.content:
The holiday season is a wild time.

Imagine spending days battling to finalize the last features. You’re feeling doubly satisfied because you managed to finish just in time for your long-awaited trip to the mountains. With a big grin on your face, you wander through forests, meadows, and bushes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/d97954fd5931bc4a113b7033becf281553a60128.jpg[/img]
Then, out of nowhere, you see it—a beautiful, patch of land. It’s on the edge of a plot, by some fence, in the middle of nowhere... And you immediately know you have to add this as a preset. This is what’s been missing from Outside the Block. You quickly snap pictures and start brainstorming. The rest of the trip is ruined. All you can think about is the clay, the round stones, and the tangled tufts of thin green grass.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/3ec7c6976bee93130d4d30ed9083312ed8346c56.jpg[/img]
You start scheming, drawing diagrams on napkins in restaurants, and jotting notes on your phone. You keep scrolling through the photos, searching for every detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/217cfdab755a2ffbb4163e46d5f0ffef67332513.jpg[/img]
When you get back home, you dive into implementing the first version. Then, you sit down and cry because it doesn’t look right. The grass is too thick, the soil’s color is off. You’re down for two days, even though this wasn’t something you needed to do at all. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/cda6a5d447f4cc617f63b02042186fadecb16879.gif[/img]

You feel frustrated for a moment, but then you sit down, make adjustments, and in the end, you basically rework everything. A few days later, you’re exhausted, yet it finally works—just in time for your next trip. Now, though, you realize that trip won’t bring you joy either, as you’ll inevitably spot something new you’ll want to turn into a preset.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/b18a7ab5521562a1224a41191913af42c8c187d6.png[/img]

I guess true relaxation is just another challenge to overcome…
But hey, at least it gives me new ideas!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/c0ad8ff305e92f45015492156dda650ddb6d1cfa.gif[/img]

The preliminary sketches evoke a mix of optimism (for the final outcome) and concern (considering the additional work ahead).

notes.title: DevUpdate: Terrain Editing
notes.content:
Hello to all the fans of building, modeling, and creating!

I'm rushing with the news that yesterday I managed to complete another mini-milestone! I was able to improve the majority of the logic responsible for terrain editing. A significant change is the introduction of new brush shapes. In the previous version, I only had a square or circular brush available, which made it difficult to achieve neat, natural shapes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/5e589f6b86335183cfaf5ca087ce8049dad01d81.png[/img]

I added several presets for generating terrain. They allow the user to generate a basic terrain layout with a single click, which can be further customized. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/ae13ca68e7ebdaa0b76f0ba9eed7c1bebdd356df.gif[/img]

I have also made some improvements to the way epoxy resin interacts with the terrain. Now, when pouring the diorama, the grass is automatically removed, and the appropriate texture is applied. Additionally, you have the freedom to blend this texture into any part of the terrain, resulting in a visually captivating and diverse landscape.

Next on my to-do list is expanding the tools for taking screenshots. As everyone knows, there's nothing more enjoyable in creating dioramas than sharing your artistic achievements with others!

Take care, and talk to you soon!

notes.title: Hello!
notes.content:
Greetings to all the fans of building, modeling, and creating!

My name is Michał, and for over a decade, I've worked as a 3D artist for video games, exploring various topics related to the environment such as architecture, modular solutions, and procedural generation.
Outside the Blocks is my hobby project, which I've been creating in my spare time. It's a tool that (I hope) will allow you to experience those amazing moments, where you look at a world that you created and think: 

"It's so lovely that I would like to live in it."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43912064/ea0944f2c242c3ef84252a4d860ac69ca3bf77b4.jpg[/img]

I'm incredibly excited to share my passion with you and can't wait to see your beautiful and creative projects! Keep an eye out for upcoming Steam posts, and don’t forget to add Outside the Blocks to your wishlists.

Take care!
